You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
# Project Kestrel: Buyer Review of Seller Positions (Wattlebridge Holdings)

**Baseline:** 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd, AUD 24.0m, debt-free/cash-free, NSW law.

## Bottom line

The Seller's package is not a fair or balanced starting point for a buyer. Read together, the Seller's clauses would leave the Buyer with almost no effective warranty protection for anything in the data room, including the very issues DD-002 to DD-012 already identify. The main problems are:

1. **Stacked disclosure, knowledge and non-reliance clauses.** Data-room disclosure (Schedule 7, DL 1.1–1.2), buyer-knowledge (cl 8.3) and exclusive-remedy/non-reliance (cl 9.3, 12.8, 20.5) combine so that known problems are disclosed, deemed known and unclaimable.
2. **Known, quantified issues are pushed into claims or post-Completion promises** rather than being resolved through price mechanics or conditions.
3. **Fundamental and title warranties are treated like ordinary warranties**, with the same cap and time limit.
4. **Conditions are weakened** (Bluefen "reasonable endeavours", Riverlark release "following Completion").

## Issue-by-issue analysis

| # | Area | Seller position | Why it departs from Buyer's interests | Pushback |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **General cap (12.1)** | AUD 4.8m (20%) | Known items alone (see table below) could approach it, and Bluefen's ~30% revenue share is unquantified. Cap also applies to fundamental and tax claims. | Keep general cap as a negotiated figure, but carve out fundamentals, title, tax and fraud from the cap. Cap fundamentals at 100% of price. Revisit general cap level once the Bluefen valuation is known. |
| 2 | **De minimis and basket (12.2)** | AUD 25k de minimis; AUD 250k deductible (only excess recoverable) | A deductible of 250k (~1% of price) means the Buyer absorbs the first AUD 250k of any claim. Claims below de minimis may not count toward the basket. | Tipping basket (first-dollar recovery once exceeded). De minimis reduced (e.g. 10k) and all claims, including below de minimis, aggregated toward the basket. Known DD matters excluded from threshold entirely. |
| 3 | **Time limits (12.3/13)** | 18 months general; limitation applies to all claims "unless expressly stated" | 18 months is short for tax (ATO amendment periods run longer) and for privacy or IP exposure that may surface later. Fundamental and title claims should not be subject to the general period. | General warranties: 24–36 months. Fundamental and title: at least 6 years (NSW limitation period for contract is 6 years; confirm interaction with the deed of indemnity). Tax: until 60 days after the ATO assessment period closes. Remove the "all claims unless stated" default reversal. |
| 4 | **Fundamental / title (cap and time)** | Same caps and limits as general warranties | Title and capacity are the foundation of the deal. Treating them like general warranties is inconsistent with the nature of the claim. | Separate regime: no general cap or basket, price cap, extended time limit. |
| 5 | **Limitations and exclusivity (9.3, 12.8, 20.5)** | Apply to "all Claims of any nature" | Would capture fraud, title and fundamental claims, and possibly specific indemnities. Exclusive remedy would also restrict rights under statute. | Carve-outs for fraud, wilful concealment, title, fundamental warranties, tax indemnity and specific indemnities. Confirm exclusive remedy does not restrict rights under the Corporations Act or ACL that cannot be contracted out of. Non-reliance should not cover the Seller's express warranties in the SPA. |
| 6 | **Disclosure (Schedule 7; DL 1.1–1.2)** | General disclosure of the entire data room, Accounts, statutory registers and public records | Converts the data room into a blanket disclosure against every warranty. Buyer cannot know what it is accepting. Data room is also cut off at 22 Sept 2026, about six weeks before today. | Delete general disclosure. Disclosure only against specific warranties, fairly disclosed and specifically described. Accounts disclosed only against the specific warranties about the Accounts. Bring disclosure down to signing and Completion. |
| 7 | **Buyer knowledge (cl 8.3)** | No claim for any matter the Buyer or its advisers knew, including matters discoverable from data room or public records | This is anti-sandbagging. Combined with DL 1.1, it would bar claims on DD-002 to DD-012 and on anything discoverable in public records. Buyer's advisers' knowledge is imputed to Buyer. Under NSW law, a clause like this would likely be enforced as written. | Delete 8.3. Insert pro-sandbagging wording: Buyer's rights are unaffected by its knowledge. Known issues are handled through specific indemnities and price adjustments, not warranty claims. |
| 8 | **Bluefen consent (cl 3/6.3; DL 2)** | Reasonable endeavours; treated as satisfied on delivery of consent. Consent not yet obtained; conditions in cl 11.3 not satisfied. | Bluefen is ~AUD 3.6m revenue (~30%). Loss would be a valuation event. "Reasonable endeavours" weakens the obligation. Consent alone may not satisfy conditions in 11.3. | Consent as a condition precedent to Completion, in agreed form, with all 11.3 conditions satisfied. If Buyer waives, a specific indemnity or price adjustment for lost revenue or termination. Seller must procure, not merely endeavour. |
| 9 | **Riverlark (cl 2/7; DL 3)** | AUD 3.2m outstanding; release "following Completion" | This is debt. On a debt-free basis it must come off the price at Completion. Post-Completion release leaves the Buyer funding a lender's lien over the Company's assets and shares. Change of control under 8.1 needs addressing. | Payoff letter and security release (including PPSR discharge and any share charge) delivered at Completion. Repayment funded from the price per funds flow. Confirm change-of-control waiver. |
| 10 | **Ironquay IP (cl 11.1; DL 4)** | Indemnity limited to SOW3 payment; "adequate" | 180k open under SOW3; project materials transfer only on payment (cl 7.3). No receipt or assignment in data room. Indemnity does not cover other Ironquay claims or IP ownership. | Seller to pay or fund the 180k before Completion (or deduct as debt-like). Confirmatory assignment and release of project materials at Completion. Specific IP indemnity covering all Ironquay claims and ownership, not only SOW3. IP warranties not limited by this clause. |
| 11 | **Employee bonuses (DL 5; funds flow)** | AUD 420k conditional bonuses excluded from funds flow; "a matter for the Seller" | These are debt-like and arise from pre-Completion arrangements. Excluding them from funds flow means Buyer may fund them. On-costs (payroll tax, superannuation) are unquantified. | Treat as Seller cost or deduct from price as debt-like, including employer on-costs. Funds flow to itemise. Seller to warrant the complete list of change-of-control and transaction bonuses. |
| 12 | **Privacy incident (cl 4.6/Sch 6; DL 6)** | "Preliminary operational matter, not expected to be material" | Export of ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). Unauthorised access not excluded. Notification may be required under the Privacy Act 1988 (Cth) NDB scheme. Revenue implies turnover above the small-business threshold, so the Act is likely to apply; confirm. Investigation unfinished, so exposure is unknown. | Pre-Completion forensic investigation and written conclusion on notification. Specific indemnity for all costs (investigation, notification, regulatory, class-related, remediation), uncapped or at a separate cap. Privacy and data warranties. Seller to notify OAIC and individuals if required, with Buyer approval of communications. Escrow or retention sized to exposure until investigation concludes. |
| 13 | **Supplier renewals (DL 8)** | 3 × AUD 110k (AUD 330k aggregate), "ordinary course" | Disclosure does not say whether they are unavoidable, terminable or accrued. Multi-year commitments could be an undisclosed liability. | Full copies of contracts and terms. Confirm which are accrued or committed for pre-Completion periods (debt-like or Seller cost). Interim covenant: no renewal or new commitment above a threshold without Buyer consent. |
| 14 | **Office lease (DL 7)** | Notification obligation; not described as landlord consent for share sale | Ambiguous. If consent is required and not obtained, there is a breach risk. | Lease review. Confirm whether change of control triggers consent or notice. If consent required, make it a condition or specific indemnity. Landlord estoppel recommended. |
| 15 | **Mossvale (DL 9)** | Assignment restriction; no consent required merely for share sale | Stated "not required", but the Buyer should verify rather than accept. | Legal review of the provision, including change-of-control language. Confirm no consent is required and get written confirmation if any doubt. |
| 16 | **Title (DL 10; DD-012)** | Share register shows Harbourglass as 100% holder | A register extract does not prove title. The Buyer has not verified its own position. | Title warranty (fundamental). ASIC company extract, original share certificates or holding statements, executed transfer forms, and PPSR search for any charge over the shares. Confirm no encumbrance or pre-emptive rights. |
| 17 | **Tax and IP (general regime)** | Warranties "settled" under general regime | Tax and IP are not settled. They are subject to the cap, basket and 18-month limit. | Pre-Completion tax indemnity (not subject to basket, de minimis or general cap). Tax warranties with a longer time limit. Tax DD to be completed. IP warranties and IP chain-of-title checks. |
| 18 | **Share, bonus and supplier totals** | "Agreed price mechanics" | The funds flow does not reflect bonuses or Riverlark release as price items. | Full reconciliation of price mechanics to the debt-free/cash-free definitions. Locked-box or completion-accounts alignment confirmed. |

## Quantifying the exposure

These figures are from the Seller's documents and have not been independently verified.

- **Price-mechanic items (should reduce price, not be claims):** Riverlark ~AUD 3.2m (debt); bonuses AUD 420k plus on-costs (debt-like).
- **Claim-type items (currently known and quantified):** Ironquay AUD 180k; supplier renewals AUD 330k (ordinary-course status unconfirmed).
- **Unquantified:** Bluefen (~AUD 3.6m revenue, about 30%); privacy incident; lease consent; Mossvale.

Under the Seller's proposed terms, the claim-type items (~AUD 510k) fall within the AUD 250k deductible only partly, and are then reduced by the buyer-knowledge bar. In practice, the Buyer would recover little of any of them.

**Point to note:** W&I insurance, if considered, will exclude known DD matters. These items need to be handled through specific indemnities, escrow or retention and price adjustment, not insurance.

## Suggested retention or escrow

Once the privacy investigation and Bluefen consent position are clearer, size an escrow or retention to cover the unquantified exposures for 18–24 months. A figure in the low millions is likely needed; the precise amount depends on the Bluefen valuation impact and the forensic findings, and should be set with the deal team's financial advisers.

## Information gaps to close before signing

1. Bluefen clause 11.2 and 11.3 conditions, and the Bluefen valuation impact if consent is refused.
2. Riverlark payoff figure, security documents, PPSR search results, change-of-control terms.
3. Ironquay SOW3 status, all other SOWs, IP chain of title.
4. Full bonus schedule with change-of-control terms and on-costs.
5. Privacy investigation report: scope, access logs, notification assessment.
6. Supplier contract terms and renewal dates.
7. Office lease and Mossvale agreements in full.
8. Share certificates, transfer forms, ASIC extract, PPSR search.
9. Bring-down of the data room and disclosure to a current date (currently 22 Sept 2026; today is 5 Nov 2026).

## Summary of recommendations (priority order)

1. **Reject general disclosure** of the data room, Accounts and public records (Sch 7; DL 1.1–1.2). Disclosure against specific warranties only.
2. **Delete the buyer-knowledge bar (cl 8.3)** and insert pro-sandbagging wording.
3. **Carve out fraud, title, fundamentals, tax and specific indemnities** from the cap, basket, time limits, exclusive remedy and non-reliance (cl 9.3, 12.1–12.8, 13, 20.5).
4. **Separate fundamental and title regime:** cap at price, 6-year limit.
5. **Tipping basket**, lower de minimis, all claims count toward basket; no "unless stated" default reversal on time limits.
6. **Resolve Riverlark and bonuses through price mechanics** at Completion, not post-Completion promises.
7. **Make Bluefen consent a condition precedent**, with all conditions satisfied; specific indemnity or price adjustment if waived.
8. **Ironquay:** pay or deduct the 180k; confirmatory assignment and release at Completion; full IP indemnity.
9. **Privacy incident:** completed forensic investigation, specific uncapped (or separately capped) indemnity, escrow until resolved.
10. **Supplier renewals, lease and Mossvale:** full documents, interim covenants, consent confirmations.
11. **Tax indemnity** outside the general regime; tax DD completed.
12. **Title:** ASIC extract, original certificates, transfer forms, PPSR search, fundamental title warranty.
13. **Escrow or retention** sized to unquantified exposures, held for 18–24 months.
14. **Bring-down** of disclosure and data room to signing and Completion.

## Caveats

- This is a commercial and legal issues review based solely on the Seller's documents. I have not verified any fact stated in them.
- NSW and Commonwealth law points (limitation periods, enforceability of non-reliance and buyer-knowledge clauses, interaction with ACL and Corporations Act misleading-conduct provisions, Privacy Act notification obligations, proportionate liability under the Civil Liability Act 2002 (NSW)) should be confirmed by Australian counsel before the mark-up goes out.
- Tax, payroll and superannuation on-cost figures require input from the deal's tax advisers.
=== END ADVICE ===
